rows.text: Front springs at the softest setting the car allows.

rows.text: Rear at 50-60 % of the car's range, for maximum rotation.

rows.text: Rear at the softest setting for traction, or 20-40 % of the range for rotation.

rows.text: Rear at the softest setting too, to prevent oversteer into corners. Raise the rear only once the car is stable on entry.

source.title: DG Edge: Understanding Natural Frequency in Gran Turismo 7

rows.text: As a default, run the rear slightly stiffer than the front; match overall stiffness to the downforce level and tyre compound.

rows.text: Front softer than rear improves rotation, stability and predictability in most cars.

rows.text: Soft front with a stiff rear rotates in every phase of the corner.
rows.tradeoff: can turn into oversteer if overdone; suits cars that are stable on the throttle

source.title: DG Edge: Understanding Natural Frequency in Gran Turismo 7

rows.text: Soft front and soft rear is a stable platform with good traction out of corners.
rows.tradeoff: gives up some rotation; suits cars that rotate well but snap on the throttle

source.title: DG Edge: Understanding Natural Frequency in Gran Turismo 7

rows.text: Stiff front with a soft rear is not advised: it kills rotation. Correct oversteer with anti-roll bars and dampers instead.

source.title: DG Edge: Understanding Natural Frequency in Gran Turismo 7

source.title: DG Edge: Understanding Natural Frequency in Gran Turismo 7

rows.text: Start with initial torque low.

rows.text: Set it as high as you are comfortable with, for predictable rotation on the power.

source.title: DG Edge: Understanding Limited Slip Differential (LSD) in Gran Turismo 7

rows.text: A fully open differential is stable and does not snap.
rows.tradeoff: less drive out of corners; the inside wheel spins

source.title: DG Edge: Understanding Limited Slip Differential (LSD) in Gran Turismo 7

source.title: DG Edge: Understanding Limited Slip Differential (LSD) in Gran Turismo 7

source.title: DG Edge: Understanding Limited Slip Differential (LSD) in Gran Turismo 7

rows.tradeoff: less rotation out of the corner

rows.tradeoff: less rotation out of the corner

rows.text: Too much damping at one end causes chatter and a lack of grip at the other end; keep compression and expansion in balance.

rows.text: For racing, expansion (rebound) is set higher than compression.
